correctness.rationale: Finite-support norming, disjoint translated input blocks and disjoint finite truncations of the translated output give an almost-full-norm lower-bound subspace. An explicit blockwise rank-one projection proves this subspace is 1-complemented. The witness gives exact distances to SS, FSS and compact operators and the Bernstein/approximation equalities; finite-codimensional intersection and a separate uniform-tail quotient argument establish the Gelfand and Kolmogorov equalities. Endpoint p=1 and c_0 estimates were checked separately.

originality.rationale: Classical compact-convolution and cross-space strict-singularity work is treated as prior art. Karlovych--Shargorodsky (2024) already proves maximal noncompactness for broad translation-invariant sequence-space operators on Z^d, so no novelty is claimed for essential-norm/maximal-noncompactness equality. Searches did not locate the combined exact all-n Bernstein/Gelfand/Kolmogorov/approximation profile, exact FSS/SS distances, or explicit 1-complemented almost-norming witness for l_p(G) and c_0(G) over arbitrary infinite discrete groups. Residual risk remains because the closest 2024 source was not exhaustively inspected at full-text theorem level and older multiplier literature may contain equivalent reformulations.

value.rationale: The theorem determines four classical s-number scales exactly, separates the result from ordinary maximal noncompactness through Bernstein and strict-singularity information, and supplies a reusable complemented-subspace mechanism valid for arbitrary infinite discrete groups.
